claims.claim_text: The indexed First Lieutenant Michael J Novosel is a high-confidence match to the Army aviator documented by the U.S. Army and Novosel Foundation.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact distinctive name, first-lieutenant rank, 1943 chronology, and explicit four-month OSS special-duty account align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the distinctive exact name, indexed rank, and source-specific OSS chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: The sources place Army air service from 1941 and four months of OSS special duty in 1943.
claims.match_notes: The official Army biography corroborates his 1941 Army entry; the foundation biography supplies the explicit OSS chronology.

claims.claim_text: Michael J Novosel was already serving as an Army air officer immediately before his four months of OSS special duty in 1943.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Promoted to First Lieutenant in 1943, he spent 4 months on special duty with the Office of Strategic Services
claims.evidence_paraphrase: He entered Army air service in 1941, was commissioned in 1942, promoted in 1943, and then served four months on OSS special duty.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the distinctive name, matching indexed rank, official Army biography, and explicit OSS chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded: continuous Army air-service chronology leads directly into the four-month 1943 OSS assignment.
claims.match_notes: This is a military assignment, not a civilian employer. The source wording Army Air Corps is preserved while the 1943 canonical component is United States Army Air Forces.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Edly D Nupen is a high-confidence match to Edly Daniel Nupen in a Little Norway roster and an official 1953 registration report.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The distinctive indexed name and middle initial expand consistently to Edly Daniel Nupen in independent wartime and official postwar sources.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from a distinctive exact surname and given name, compatible middle name, and two independent full-name sources.
claims.temporal_assessment: The wartime roster establishes Little Norway association during 1940-1945, but its sequence relative to OSS service is unresolved.
claims.match_notes: The postwar Justice Department source corroborates identity only; its public-relations work is not represented as pre-OSS employment.

claims.claim_text: A 1947 trade-journal profile of designer Dorothy Q. Noyes is a plausible identity and chronology lead, not a settled match to the index record.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Miss Noyes has been a free lance designer and touring architectural reporter
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The profile names a designer with the exact distinctive name and prior National Housing information work, but supplies no OSS identifier or dates.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Plausible exact-name candidate requiring Box 564 corroboration; the civilian SP-6 grade alone is insufficient.
claims.temporal_assessment: The source is retrospective in 1947 and does not establish whether the cited roles preceded OSS service.
claims.match_notes: Retained privately as a lead. No organization, occupation, or employer is published as fact until identity and chronology are corroborated.
